Interpret the condition as follows: starting at 1 and going around the circle in either direction, the numbers increase until they reach 7. So the two arcs from 1 to 7 are each increasing.

Fix 1 at a position, so rotations are not counted separately. The number 7 is the largest, so it must be the endpoint where the two arcs meet.

Each of the numbers 2 through 6 lies on exactly one of the two arcs. Once we decide which arc each number goes on, the order within each arc is forced, because it must be increasing. Each of the 5 numbers has 2 choices of arc, which gives 2^5 = 32 arrangements.

Reflections are counted as different arrangements, since choosing the complementary set of arcs gives a distinct arrangement.

ANSWER: 32
